STATUS: NOT STARTED. Unsigned, deliberately queued behind 2b16-9be0-a8f5-41d9.

Reparented under epic e369-a449-4773-48fb by operator ruling (all three J11-surfaced defects gate that
epic). File impact is already declared, so the plan review can be run immediately — but see below.

**DO NOT START THIS BEFORE 2b16 LANDS.** Both tickets modify `inbound_differ.py`; running them in
parallel would collide. 2b16 is claimed and ready to implement; land it first.

THE DEFECT, traced: an inbound parent CLEAR is dropped by TWO independent layers —
`fetcher.py:508-511` omits an absent parent from the snapshot, so the clear is invisible downstream,
and `inbound_differ.py:266-270` then refuses `parent_id=None` so nothing is emitted. The APPLY layer
is already capable of handling it, which is what makes this purely a detection gap.

A LIVE ORACLE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS EXPECTED RED:
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`, asserting
`fields.parent` / `.parent_id` is falsy after the parent was proven present. Do NOT edit or invert it.

ONE PLATFORM UNKNOWN the harness must settle, recorded by the agent that wrote the cell: whether DC
accepts nulling a sub-task's `fields.parent` at all. The cell reports that case as an explicit
`SETUP FAILED` message, so the first red will name which of the two situations it is rather than
looking like a bridge defect. Read that before concluding the fix is wrong.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## MUTATION LEDGER — six mutations, all RED, and the load-bearing one proves the guards carry the weight

Run by the orchestrator INLINE rather than by a subagent: two agents stalled on this worktree (watchdog,
600s no progress), and the second stalled at exactly this step. Each mutation was applied to the
IMPLEMENTED source, the module re-run, then the file restored from the byte-verified backups in
`/tmp/88d9-bak/` — **`git checkout --` was never used.** Every mutation was verified to have actually
applied before its verdict was believed (an unapplied mutation yields a false GREEN, so the harness
asserts the write landed). Baseline and post-restore both **16 passed**.

Module: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_parent_clear_88d9.py` (16 tests).

| mutation | file | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **M6 UNCONDITIONAL CLEAR** — all three guards stripped at once | inbound_fields.py | **4 failed, 12 passed** |
| M1 layer-1 revert: a None parent leaves the field ABSENT again | fetcher.py | 3 failed, 13 passed |
| M2 UNOBSERVED treated as NO_PARENT | inbound_fields.py | 2 failed, 14 passed |
| M3 UNRESOLVABLE treated as NO_PARENT | inbound_fields.py | 1 failed, 15 passed |
| M4 managed gate bypassed | inbound_fields.py | 1 failed, 15 passed |
| M5 `"parent": "parent_id"` removed from `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` | inbound_differ.py | 2 failed, 14 passed |

No verdict was an `AttributeError` / `ImportError` / `TypeError`, so every RED is an oracle refusing
behaviour rather than a mutation breaking wiring.

### M6 IS THE RESULT THAT MATTERS — an unconditional clear is a DATA-LOSS BUG that the happy path CANNOT SEE

FAILED under M6 — exactly and only the four guard oracles:
    test_unobserved_parent_emits_no_clear
    test_degraded_parent_map_emits_no_clear
    test_unresolvable_parent_key_emits_nothing
    test_unmanaged_parent_is_adopted_not_clobbered

STILL PASSING under M6 — including **both** oracles one would naively trust:
    test_observed_parentless_emits_the_clear          <- the HAPPY PATH
    test_end_to_end_a_removed_jira_parent_leaves_parent_id_empty   <- the END-TO-END oracle
    (plus test_unchanged_parent_does_not_churn, test_reparent_still_emits_the_new_parent,
     test_never_parented_issue_never_emits_a_parent_mutation, test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_
     suppresses_the_clear, test_outbound_parent_translates_to_the_inbound_parent_id_name, and 5 more)

So a fix that clears the parent unconditionally — deleting local parents off truncated and failed reads —
**passes the happy-path AND the end-to-end assertion.** Only the guards catch it. That is the whole
argument for the guard oracles existing, demonstrated rather than asserted.

Verbatim guard messages:

    a parent clear was emitted for an issue the parent map NEVER MENTIONED — a truncated or
    cross-project read would silently delete the local parent: {'DC-1': {'parent_id': None}}

    a FAILED parent-map read (the {} degradation contract) cleared the local parent — the exact
    silent data loss this ticket exists to prevent: {'DC-1': {'parent_id': None}}

    an UNRESOLVABLE Jira parent key emitted a parent_id mutation. Jira has a parent — it is merely
    unbound this pass — so neither a clear nor a set is correct

    an UNMANAGED parent was cleared. rebar never managed this ref, so its local presence is not
    evidence we ever pushed it and the clear clobbers local state

### The two ACs that are easiest to under-deliver are both satisfied

 * **End-to-end**: `test_end_to_end_a_removed_jira_parent_leaves_parent_id_empty` exists and asserts the
   REDUCED TICKET's `parent_id` is empty — not merely the differ's output. (And note it is NOT sufficient
   on its own: M6 shows it passing while the code is a data-loss bug.)
 * **No hand-mirrored production copy**: layer 1 was EXTRACTED as
   `fetcher.merge_parent_map(snapshot, parent_map)`, a directly-callable production helper whose docstring
   states the three-state contract, and the tests drive THAT. This is the lesson bought by 2b16, whose G1
   evidence rests on `_enrich_like_fetcher` — a byte-faithful hand copy that will silently drift. M1
   mutating the real helper and turning 3 tests RED is the proof the tests are wired to production code.

### Implementation shape, for the record

`classify_inbound_parent` returns one of four explicit states — `PARENT_UNOBSERVED` (no `parent` key),
`PARENT_NO_PARENT` (key PRESENT and falsy: queried, Jira genuinely has none), `PARENT_RESOLVED`,
`PARENT_UNRESOLVABLE` — and `diff_inbound_parent` emits the clear only for `PARENT_NO_PARENT`, gated on the
shared `should_propagate_removal`, the same provider-agnostic predicate the outbound side wraps as
`_parent_clear_is_managed`. Reused, not re-invented.

LOC, all under the 800 cap: **inbound_differ.py 797 → 773 (NET NEGATIVE — layer 2 was extracted, not
inlined, which was required since it had only 3 lines of headroom after 2b16), inbound_fields.py 247 → 351,
fetcher.py 670 → 707.**

### KNOWN BLIND SPOT, recorded not hidden

`add_managed_ref` is folded by the parent-set EVENT (`reducer/_processors.py:90,528`), so "managed" means
the ref was set LOCALLY — it does NOT prove Jira ever had that parent. The same-pass suppression closes
this in a healthy pass, and it genuinely fires for parent because `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` maps
`"parent" → "parent_id"` (M5 proves a test catches that entry's removal). The residual window is a DEGRADED
pass — outbound not writing the parent while inbound proceeds. **Read 2b16's latest comment before
assuming this suppression is enough: on the LINK side the analogous same-pass guard turned out to suppress
every legitimate peer-deletion mirror.** The parent case differs (an outbound parent SET is emitted only
for an epic parent, per 39c1's disjoint gates, so it does not fire on every peer clear the way a link ADD
does) — but that asymmetry is a reason to verify on the harness, not to assume.

comments.body:
## CHANGE 1288 TOOK `Verified -1` — a REAL failure, and it is MY process error: I pushed without the consumer sweep

`LLM-Review +1` (PASS, 3 advisory). CI run 30824364505 failed on **all four pytest legs** — so not the
stale-base missing-file trap (that fails a single script step) and not a cancellation. Two tests, both in
`tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/jira_contract/test_jira_fixtures.py`:

    test_fake_routes_fixtures_through_production_fetch
      E  AssertionError: top-level issue should carry no parent key      (:86)
    test_fetch_snapshot_conforms_to_schema

**Cause: layer 1's explicit `None` violates the declared snapshot shape, and I never finished the
consumer sweep before pushing.** That sweep is one of this ticket's acceptance criteria; the first agent
stalled before it and I ran only `tests/unit/.../diffing/` (287 passed) rather than a slice wide enough to
reach the integration contract. The AC existed precisely to catch this and I skipped it.

Both failures are the SAME root fact, in two places:
 * `_snapshot_schema.py:110` declares `parent: JiraParent`, documented at `:42` and `:122` as `{"key": str}`.
   An explicit `None` is not that shape, so the conformance test fails.
 * `test_jira_fixtures.py:86` asserts `"parent" not in epic` — "top-level issue should carry no parent key".

### This is NOT a reason to abandon the explicit-None design — the same test already blesses the pattern

Two lines above the failing assertion, the same test asserts
`epic.get("issuelinks") == []` with the comment *"authoritative EMPTY links list, no parent"*. So the
suite ALREADY distinguishes an authoritative empty value from an absent one — for issuelinks. Parent was
simply never given its half, which is this ticket's whole thesis, and is the same
"one side got the treatment, the other didn't" shape as the five DC defects this epic has fixed.

### The remedy — two edits, and the new assertion is STRONGER than the one it replaces

 1. `_snapshot_schema.py` — widen `parent` to `JiraParent | None` and document `None` as the
    AUTHORITATIVE-PARENTLESS shape (key PRESENT, value falsy), distinct from the key being ABSENT, which
    remains "never queried". Update the `:42` / `:122` shape notes so the table does not go stale — the
    docstring IS the contract other readers work from.
 2. `test_jira_fixtures.py:86` — invert PRESERVING INTENT, and record why in the assertion message. The
    intent is "a top-level issue must not be misreported as having a parent"; that intent is fully kept,
    and the replacement asserts MORE: `"parent" in epic` **and** `epic.get("parent") is None` — i.e. the
    issue was queried AND is authoritatively parentless. The old form could not tell that from a failed or
    truncated read, which is the exact ambiguity this ticket exists to remove. Per this epic's own lesson,
    an existing test that pins the defect gets inverted with its intent preserved and the reason recorded
    in the docstring — it is not deleted, and it is not "fixed" by weakening the new behaviour.

**File impact must be widened to include both files** before re-implementing, and the plan re-reviewed.

### What I got wrong, plainly

I ran a targeted module and treated 287 green as sufficient to push. The ticket's consumer-sweep AC named
exactly this risk — "a consumer using `\"parent\" in fields` or indexing `fields[\"parent\"]` WOULD change
behaviour; grep for both forms" — and `test_jira_fixtures.py:86` uses the `in` form. A grep for
`"parent" not in` / `"parent" in` across `tests/` would have found it in seconds. Do that sweep before the
next push, and run at least `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/` as well as the unit slice.

The implementation itself is unchanged and still correct; the mutation ledger recorded above stands. This
is a contract-surface omission, not a defect in the two layers.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== INCIDENT: THIS FIX DESTROYED DATA IN PRODUCTION. REVERTED. 63 TICKETS AFFECTED. ===

Change 1288 (`6baa030460`) merged at 15:34 UTC. The scheduled production bridge ran at 15:34:51 and its
reconcile pass wrote, between **15:37:59.284 and 15:38:10.110 UTC, 63 EDIT events of
`{"fields":{"parent_id":""}}`, author `reconciler`, across 63 tickets** — clearing the local parent of
every one. Reported by the operator, who saw seven of them in one epic (172e, 7761, 7b22, cb6f, cc33,
d23e, f844; descendant count 43 -> 37). The true blast radius is 63, spanning ~20 parents: `60ce` (8
children), `297d` (7), `eb58` (6), `3c55`/`5a52`/`87ab` (4 each), and others.

**It was the PRODUCTION JIRA CLOUD BRIDGE, not the DC harness.** `reconcile-bridge.yml` runs `*/20`.
So this was never a DC-only change — it is shared core, and Cloud is where it fired.

--- MECHANISM: THE DOCSTRING NAMED THE BLIND SPOT AND THEN RESTED THE FEATURE ON A GUARD THAT CANNOT FIRE ---

`diff_inbound_parent` (`inbound_fields.py`) clears the local parent when the peer is OBSERVED parentless
and `should_propagate_removal("parent", ...)` is True. Its own docstring says: "`add_managed_ref` is
folded by the parent-set EVENT, so a ref is 'managed' the instant it is set LOCALLY — MANAGED does not
prove Jira ever had the parent." It then states the mitigation: "The differ's same-pass suppression
closes that", and calls the residual "a degraded pass in which outbound does not write the parent".

**That suppression can never fire.** Per [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] — CONFIRMED LIVE before this landed —
the outbound parent op is never emitted: the emit gate omits the parent unless it is an `epic`
(`outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent`, bug 8b25's hierarchy guard) while DC's `set_parent` accepts
only a SUB-TASK child. Disjoint. And on Cloud the same emit gate skips every non-epic parent. So for any
ticket whose local parent was never pushed there is NO outbound parent write to suppress against, the
clear fires, and the edge is destroyed. **The "residual window" is the normal case, on both backends.**

This is the SAME defect class I proved on 2b16 an hour earlier and recorded there: `managed_refs` answers
"did we create this ref locally", never "did the peer ever have it". Two tickets, one wrong premise. On
2b16 the accidental outbound-ADD suppression kept the feature dormant and therefore harmless; here the
equivalent suppression was structurally unreachable, so the same premise became live data loss.

--- ACTIONS TAKEN ---
 1. **`reconcile-bridge` DISABLED** (`disabled_manually`) and the in-flight pass (30829927941) cancelled.
    It runs every 20 minutes and had already run five times on this code; it would also have re-cleared
    anything repaired. One command to re-enable — do that only after the revert has landed.
 2. **REVERT pushed as Gerrit change 1292** (reverts `6baa030460` whole: 6 files, -690/+48). LLM-Review +1
    at the time of writing. Reverted whole rather than patched because the detection gap cannot be closed
    safely without positive evidence the peer once had the parent, and that is not persisted today.
 3. **Damage assessed and proved recoverable.** All 63 prior parents were recovered from the event log
    (CREATE/SNAPSHOT before the reconciler's clear) and cross-checked against live state: all 63 are
    CURRENTLY parentless and all 63 have a recovered parent, so nothing newer can be overwritten. None
    had been de-parented by a human (the walk would have flagged it). Manifest:
    `/Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/7604559b/tmp/repair.json`. Statuses: 61 closed, 1 in_progress, 1 open.
    Note a correction to the operator's report: 7b22's parent was `03b0-2290-f4f3-47a8`, not `eb58`.

--- THE REPAIR IS BLOCKED BY A CAPABILITY GAP, and I verified all four candidate routes ---
`rebar edit <child> --parent=<closed parent>` is REFUSED: "cannot re-parent to closed ticket" — the
`--parent` validation cascade in `_commands/composer.py:503-513`. 61 of the 63 parents are closed.
 * **`edit --parent` is the ONLY reparent path.** There is no `parent`/`move`/`reparent` command;
   `link`/`unlink` cover the six link relations, not hierarchy.
 * **`edit` has NO `--force`.** Zero mentions in its help; `force` does not appear in `composer.py`.
 * **`rebar revert` DOES NOT RESTORE STATE.** `process_revert` (`reducer/_processors.py:456-488`) only
   appends a record to `state["reverts"]`; the sole state effect is un-archiving on REVERT-of-ARCHIVED.
   Reverting the reconciler's EDIT would log the revert and leave `parent_id` empty. Checked, not assumed.
 * **`fsck-recover`** is git-level dangling-write recovery, not semantic repair.
 * `rebar.edit_ticket` shells out to the same CLI, so the library hits the same guard.
So rebar has no supported way to restore a parent edge onto a closed parent. The workaround —
reopen each parent, re-parent, re-close — rewrites the close records of ~20 already-signed epics and
re-runs the LLM close gate ~20 times, where a single failure leaves a previously-closed epic OPEN.

OPERATOR DIRECTION: address the root cause, not the symptom. So the repair capability is being ADDED:
`--force` on `edit`, scoped to bypass ONLY the closed-parent status check (not existence, not
self-parent, not the cycle walk), following rebar's existing `--force` idiom (`claim --force`,
`--force-close`). Repair then runs as `edit --parent=<id> --force` with no status churn and no
re-verification.

--- WHAT THIS TICKET NOW IS ---
88d9 stays OPEN. Its AC "a parent removed in Jira clears the local parent_id" is NOT satisfiable by the
approach reviewed and certified here, and the certified plan should not be re-attempted as written. The
honest fix is the same one 2b16 needs: arbitrate on the ADR-0026 per-binding BASELINE (last-synced peer
state, advanced every pass by `reconcile._advance_baselines`, absent-baseline already documented as
degrading to local-wins) so a clear fires only on POSITIVE evidence that the peer once had the parent.
See the design notes on 2b16. **And 39c1 should be re-ruled: it is no longer a theoretical
non-fail-safe divergence, it is the mechanism by which this fix destroyed 63 parent edges.**

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== RED TEST FIRST, BY OPERATOR DIRECTION — AND IT IS RED AGAINST BOTH WRONG STATES OF THE CODE ===

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_parent_clear_requires_peer_evidence.py`, committed as
**ea552f8589** on branch `fix-88d9-peer-evidence` (based on the revert `2241e3d189`). Three cells, all
driving the production entry point `compute_inbound_mutations` — never a private helper, so a moved or
missing helper reads as a failed ASSERTION rather than an AttributeError (the reverted change had
shuffled this logic between modules twice).

**MEASURED, both directions — this is the part that matters:**

  against the DEFECTIVE tree (gerrit/main @ 6baa030460, the code that caused the incident):
    FAILED test_a_parent_the_peer_never_had_is_not_cleared
      "REGRESSION -- the 63-ticket incident. A local parent rebar never pushed was cleared because it
       is in managed_refs (emitted parent_id=None)"
    1 failed, 2 passed

  against the REVERTED tree (2241e3d189, what will be on main):
    FAILED test_a_parent_the_peer_once_had_is_cleared
      "the peer's last-synced parent was DC-9 and the peer now has NONE"
    1 failed, 2 passed

So each WRONG state satisfies one half and fails the other:
 * defective  = clears a parent the peer never had  -> fails the negative cell;
 * reverted   = never clears at all                 -> fails the positive cell.
**A single assertion cannot distinguish "correct" from "one of the two failure modes."** That is
exactly how this repo has shipped oracles that could not fail (2944, 59b2, the vacuous `08-assign`
cell), and it is why the pair must not be split or trimmed to make a build green. The third cell —
`test_an_unobserved_parent_is_never_cleared_even_with_peer_evidence` — holds the fail-open read safe:
with peer evidence present, an ABSENT `parent` key must still emit nothing, because `get_parent_map`
degrades to `{}` on any REST failure and a truncated page walk simply omits issues.

--- THE FIX THE THIRD STATE REQUIRES ---

Clear only on POSITIVE evidence that the peer once carried this parent. The evidence channel is the
ADR-0026 per-binding record, which already exists, is already advanced every pass, and is already
persisted by the binding-store commit path with no new commit surface:

 1. `binding_store`: `set_peer_parent(local_id, key)` / `get_peer_parent(local_id)` on the binding
    entry — its OWN key, NOT a 6th entry in `_BASELINE_FIELDS` (that tuple is the 5-scalar
    three-way-merge vocabulary consumed by `outbound_field_diff` and `binding_walk`; widening it would
    perturb that merge). Absent = unknown = fail safe, matching the documented baseline semantics
    ("an ABSENT baseline is VALID and degrades to local-wins").
 2. `reconcile`: advance it beside `_advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:519-536`) — **only when this
    pass OBSERVED the parent key.** This is the load-bearing detail: if a fail-open read were allowed
    to overwrite a good history with "no parent", the next pass would read that as a deletion and the
    incident returns by a longer route.
 3. `inbound_fields.diff_inbound_parent`: emit the clear only when `get_peer_parent` returns a truthy
    key AND this pass observed no parent. `managed_refs` may stay as an additional gate but must never
    DECIDE — it cannot answer the question, which is the whole lesson of this incident and of 2b16.

Same shape as the arbitration 2b16 needs. One wrong premise produced two defects; one evidence channel
retires both.

--- STATUS ---
Revert 1292 has `LLM-Review +1` and is awaiting `Verified`; the production bridge stays DISABLED until
it lands. The fix is NOT pushed: a RED-only change cannot earn `Verified +1`, so it squashes with the
implementation. The store repair is settled — operator ACCEPTED the current state for the 61 closed
tickets; the two that were not closed (437c in_progress, bf03 open) were repaired with a plain
`rebar edit --parent` and verified. The missing capability is filed as idea 5992-f317-e05e-42f7
(dedicated `parent` verb with `--force`), out of scope by operator direction.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## THE FIX IS UP — Gerrit change 1296, RED-first, squashed

Revert 1292 is MERGED and verified against the tree: 'diff_inbound_parent' is ABSENT from
gerrit/main's inbound_fields.py, so main carries no parent-clear path at all. The production bridge has
been RE-ENABLED on that basis (it was disabled while the destructive code was on main).

Change **1296** ('Clear a Jira-dropped parent only on peer evidence'), rebased onto current gerrit/main,
9 files / +984 / -48. It re-applies the reverted scaffolding — the three-state parent read,
fetcher.merge_parent_map, the nullable schema, the differ wiring — and adds the evidence gate whose
absence destroyed 63 parent edges:

 * binding_store.get_peer_parent / set_peer_parent: a new key on the binding entry beside the ADR-0026
   baseline. In-memory until save(), persisted by the existing commit path, no new commit surface.
   ABSENT is VALID and fails safe to NO CLEAR, so a v1 store, a pre-field binding, an unconfirmed
   binding and an out-of-window key are all safe by construction.
 * reconcile._advance_peer_parent, called from _advance_baselines and gated on '"parent" in entry'.
   THE LOAD-BEARING LINE: a fail-open read (get_parent_map degrading to {}, a truncated page walk) must
   never overwrite a good observation with 'no parent', or the next pass reads a deletion and the
   incident returns by a longer route.
 * diff_inbound_parent declines unless get_peer_parent is truthy. managed_refs REMAINS as a further
   gate but no longer DECIDES — that is the entire lesson of this incident and of 2b16.

ROLLOUT BEHAVIOUR, stated so nobody is surprised: on the first pass after this lands, no binding has a
recorded observation, so NOTHING is cleared. Observations accumulate as passes run and the feature
becomes live per-binding. It self-heals into correctness rather than starting hot.

EVIDENCE
 * the discriminating trio ('test_parent_clear_requires_peer_evidence.py') measured RED against BOTH
   wrong states — defective tree fails the negative cell, reverted tree fails the positive cell — and
   GREEN against the fix. Recorded in the preceding comment with the exact failure strings.
 * two cells in the original module PINNED THE BUG (they asserted a clear with no peer evidence). Their

# A parent REMOVED in Jira never clears the local parent_id (inbound)

Found while writing the row-13 inbound cell of the J11 mutation table
(story 5200-e04e-246e-4aae), filed per that story's rule that a cell revealing a
product defect stops and reports. THIS TICKET NOW CARRIES THE FIX (reparented under
epic e369-a449-4773-48fb by operator ruling).

## Mechanism — TWO independent layers each drop the signal

1. THE SNAPSHOT NEVER CARRIES "no parent". The fetcher's parent enrichment merges
   `client.get_parent_map()` into the snapshot and, when the mapped parent is None,
   deliberately leaves the field ABSENT: "When parent_jira_key is None, leave the
   field absent (top-level issue) - consistent with Jira REST shape"
   (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:508-511). So an issue whose parent
   was removed looks identical to an issue that never had one.

2. THE DIFFER REFUSES TO EMIT A CLEAR. `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local` resolves
   the Jira parent to a local id and emits `changed["parent_id"]` ONLY when that
   resolution is non-None; the None case is explicitly skipped with the reason
   recorded inline: "We do NOT emit parent_id=None to avoid accidentally clearing a
   locally-set parent when we just can't resolve it yet"
   (inbound_differ.py:257-270, helper `_extract_parent_local_id` at :90-110).

The comment names the real design tension: "Jira has no parent" and "the parent key
is not bound yet" are COLLAPSED into the same None, so the differ cannot clear
without risking a spurious clear. The apply layer is already ready for the clear —
`apply_inbound_records` maps `parent_id` through `lambda v: v or ""` and its comment
says "an absent/empty parent maps to '' (clears the parent; ticket 8b25)"
(apply_inbound_records.py:361-372). Only the differ never sends it.

## Why this is a gap

Story 5200's row 13 INBOUND oracle is "`.parent_id` is null". It is unreachable
today: a de-parenting done in Jira is silently invisible to rebar, so the two
systems diverge permanently with no report.

Fixing it needs the ambiguity resolved, not just the guard removed: the parent map
must distinguish "queried and absent" from "not resolvable". The information is NOT
missing at the source — the map already returns `{key -> parent_key | None}`; it is
discarded at fetcher.py:509-511. **The Approach below resolves exactly this**, and it
is the reason this is a two-layer change rather than a one-line guard removal.

## Expected failure

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`
asserts `.parent_id` is empty after the DC parent is cleared. It should go RED on
the harness until this is addressed. Note that cell asserts the DC-side clear as its
own SETUP step, so "Data Center refused to null a sub-task's parent" is reported
distinctly from this gap.

## Approach

Two layers each drop the signal, so both must change. The design problem is the same one
`2b16-9be0-a8f5-41d9` faces in the link direction and is solved the same way: an inbound CLEAR is a
WRITE that destroys local data, so it may only fire on POSITIVE evidence that Jira was asked and
answered "no parent" — never on the mere absence of data.

**This epic has already settled the predicate shape, in its own story 5200.** That story's first draft
of the parent-cell wait helper took a predicate over `mapping[key]`, and `get_parent_map` has a
degradation contract — any REST failure logs a warning and returns `{}`
(`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:520-527`). So "no parent for this key" and "the parent-map read
failed entirely" were indistinguishable, and the wait would have been satisfied by a broken read. It
was fixed before landing to `lambda m: key in m and not m[key]` — **key PRESENT with a falsy value**.
That is exactly the distinction both layers below need; the fix is to carry it into production code
rather than only into the test helper.

### Layer 1 — the snapshot must record "queried, and there is no parent"

`fetcher.py:508-511` merges `client.get_parent_map()` and, when the mapped parent is None, deliberately
leaves the field ABSENT ("consistent with Jira REST shape"). Make it explicit instead:
`snapshot[snap_key]["parent"] = None` — key PRESENT, value None.

Why this is safe for every existing consumer: all of them read the field with `.get("parent")` and
branch on falsiness, so an explicit None is indistinguishable from absent to them —
`inbound_differ.py:104` (`if not parent_raw: return None`), `inbound_fields.py:229`,
`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:519` (`isinstance(parent_raw, dict)`),
`apply_inbound_records.py:186`, and `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:518`. Only the new removal
path uses `"parent" in jira_fields`. **Verify this list against the tree before relying on it** — a
consumer that used `"parent" in fields` or indexed `fields["parent"]` would change behaviour.

The loop only visits keys `get_parent_map` returned AND that are in the snapshot, so an issue the map
never mentioned still gets NO key — which is the unobserved case, and a total read failure returns `{}`
and therefore clears nothing. Both degrade safe.

### Layer 2 — the differ must distinguish THREE states, not two

`_diff_jira_vs_local` (inbound_differ.py:257-270) resolves through `_extract_parent_local_id` (:90-110),
which returns None for three different situations collapsed into one, then refuses to emit. Replace the
two-state read with a three-state one:

| snapshot state | meaning | action |
|---|---|---|
| `"parent"` NOT in `jira_fields` | never queried / read failed / truncated | **skip** — emit nothing |
| `"parent"` present and falsy | queried; Jira has NO parent | **emit the clear** (gated below) |
| `"parent"` present with a key that resolves | Jira parent known | set/compare as today |
| `"parent"` present with a key that does NOT resolve | parent not yet bound | **skip** — retry next pass |

The existing inline comment ("We do NOT emit parent_id=None to avoid accidentally clearing a
locally-set parent when we just can't resolve it yet") is correct about the hazard and wrong only in
that it treats one unresolvable case as if it covered all of them. Preserve its intent — the
unresolvable case still skips — while letting the observed-absent case through.

### The gates on the clear

- **MANAGED.** Only clear a parent rebar MANAGED: `should_propagate_removal("parent", local_parent_id,
  local_ticket)` from `rebar.reducer._managed_refs`. The outbound direction already wraps this exact
  predicate as `_parent_clear_is_managed` (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:296`), whose docstring
  states the symmetric intent outright — "a parent a human set directly in Jira (one local never had)
  would be clobbered instead of ADOPTED inbound". Reuse the predicate; do not invent a second rule.
- **KNOWN BLIND SPOT, recorded not hidden.** `add_managed_ref` is folded by the LINK/parent-set event
  processors (`reducer/_processors.py:90,411,528`), so a ref is "managed" the instant it is set
  LOCALLY — it does NOT prove we pushed it to Jira. `seed_managed_refs_from_current` compounds this for
  pre-feature tickets. So MANAGED alone does not establish Jira ever had the parent.
- **SAME-PASS SUPPRESSION closes that blind spot, and here it already works.** `inbound_differ.py:667`
  drops any inbound `changed` field the same pass's outbound is writing
  (`changed = {k: v for k, v in changed.items() if k not in ob_entry["fields"]}`), and the outbound→
  inbound name translation `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` at :495-498 **does** contain
  `"parent": "parent_id"` — verified, so the suppression genuinely fires for parent rather than missing
  on a name mismatch. A locally-set parent that outbound is pushing this pass is therefore not cleared
  inbound. **Pin this with a test**, because it is currently load-bearing by inheritance and a future
  edit to that map would silently remove the protection.
  Residual window, stated plainly: a degraded pass in which outbound does not write the parent (skipped,
  disabled, or failed) while inbound proceeds.

### The emit, end to end

Emit `changed["parent_id"] = None`. The apply layer is ALREADY ready: `apply_inbound_records.py:361-372`
maps `parent_id` through `lambda v: v or ""` under `if _fname in fields`, and its comment says "an
absent/empty parent maps to '' (clears the parent; ticket 8b25)". So no apply-layer change is expected
— but **prove it**, do not assume it: the mutation must be followed differ → `InboundMutation.fields`
→ `run_differs` payload → `apply_inbound` → the reduced ticket's `parent_id` is empty. A `None` value
is exactly the kind of thing an intermediate `if v` or a falsy-filtering dict comprehension drops
silently, which is this epic's signature failure mode (this is how `2b16` turned out to need a second
file). If something does strip it, that file joins the scope and the ticket records why.

**Alternative rejected: compare against the previous peer snapshot.** Present-before / absent-now is the
textbook signal and would retire the MANAGED blind spot, but `reconcile._write_prev_snapshot_key_set`
persists `{jira_key: {}}` — key membership only, no fields — as of `6cdd4b00d9`. Using it means adding
a new persisted artifact with its own migration and truncation semantics, larger than this defect
warrants.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — layer 1 (explicit None for a queried-absent parent).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — layer 2 + the MANAGED gate.
  **CRITICAL, CHANGED AFTER 2b16: this file is at 797/800 once change 1276 lands — THREE lines of
  headroom, not 82.** 2b16 grew it 718 → 817 (over the cap) and had to shed the observed-peer-link set
  into `link_direction.py` to reach 797. So layer 2 CANNOT be added inline; plan the seam up front.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` — **the seam for layer 2's extraction.** It is
  247 LOC (ample room) and ALREADY reads `jira_fields.get("parent")` at :229, so parent-field extraction
  is work it already owns: this is a real call-graph seam, not a mechanical split to beat a number.
  `link_direction.py` is NOT the right home — it owns link direction, and 2b16 already left it at 89 LOC.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_parent_clear_88d9.py` (new).
- **Out of scope:** `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` (another ticket owns it);
  `apply_inbound_records.py` unless the end-to-end trace proves the `None` is dropped there.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a parent removed in Jira clears the local `parent_id`: asserted POSITIVELY EMPTY on the reduced
      ticket, never "no exception was raised"
- [ ] the clear survives END TO END — differ emit → `InboundMutation.fields` → `run_differs` payload →
      `apply_inbound` → the reduced ticket's `parent_id` is empty. A differ-boundary-only oracle does
      NOT satisfy this
- [ ] with the snapshot's `"parent"` key ABSENT (unobserved: read failure, `{}` degradation, or a
      truncated page), NO clear is emitted — simulate the real shape, including
      `get_parent_map` returning `{}`
- [ ] with `"parent"` present and falsy (queried, genuinely no parent), the clear IS emitted
- [ ] a Jira parent whose key does NOT resolve to a local id still emits NOTHING (the original guard's
      intent is preserved and independently tested)
- [ ] a parent that is not in `managed_refs` is NOT cleared, so a parent a human set directly in Jira is
      adopted rather than clobbered
- [ ] the same-pass suppression is pinned by a test: when outbound is writing `parent` in the same pass,
      the inbound clear is suppressed — asserted through `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` so a future edit
      to that map fails a test instead of silently removing the protection
- [ ] steady state does not churn: an issue that never had a parent, and one whose parent is unchanged,
      emit NO clear on repeated passes
- [ ] every existing consumer of the snapshot `parent` field is enumerated and shown unaffected by the
      explicit-None change (a grep-backed list recorded on this ticket, plus a test that a
      never-parented issue still produces no parent mutation)
- [ ] every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set MUST
      include making the clear unconditional — an unguarded clear passes the happy-path oracle while
      being a data-loss bug, so the guard oracles are the ones that protect the product
- [ ] `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is
      unmodified and turns GREEN on the harness once this lands — UNLESS it reports its explicit
      `SETUP FAILED` message, which means Data Center refused to null a sub-task's `fields.parent`. That
      is a PLATFORM finding, not this fix failing; record it and file it separately rather than
      weakening the cell
- [ ] the parent enrichment merge in `fetcher.py` is EXTRACTED into a named, directly-callable helper
      and the unit test drives THAT helper — not a hand-mirrored copy of it. **This is a lesson bought
      by 2b16**, whose equivalent guard evidence rests on `_enrich_like_fetcher`, a byte-faithful hand
      copy of `fetcher.py:592-596` written only because that merge is inline in `fetch_snapshot` and
      cannot be called directly. That copy will silently drift, and it guards the boundary between a
      truncated read and deleted local data. Do not repeat it: layer 1 is being edited here anyway, so
      extracting it is cheap now and removes the weakest link from the evidence
- [ ] `fetcher.py`, `inbound_differ.py` and `inbound_fields.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap —
      `inbound_differ.py` starts this change at 797, so its delta must be net-negative or near-zero
